title: SEBI's New Vault Rules: Enhanced Security for Gold & Silver ETFs
description: SEBI has introduced a comprehensive framework for vault managers storing physical gold and silver bullion underlying ETFs. These new rules mandate stricter st.

faq.q: What is a vault manager in the context of ETFs?
faq.a: A vault manager is an entity responsible for the secure storage and safekeeping of the physical gold or silver bullion that underlies Gold and Silver Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs). They ensure the physical assets are secure, segregated, and accounted for.

faq.q: Does this mean my physical gold jewellery or coins are also covered?
faq.a: No, these new SEBI rules specifically apply to the physical bullion held by vault managers on behalf of Gold and Silver ETFs. They do not cover personal holdings of physical gold jewellery, coins, or bars.

faq.q: How do these rules benefit me as an investor?
faq.a: These rules enhance investor protection by standardising and strengthening the security, storage, and accounting practices for the physical gold and silver backing your ETF investments. This reduces the risk of loss or fraud and increases transparency.

faq.q: Do these rules apply to both Gold and Silver ETFs?
faq.a: Yes, the new SEBI framework for vault managers applies to both Gold ETFs and Silver ETFs, ensuring a consistent standard of physical asset management across both categories of precious metal ETFs.

faq.q: Will the expense ratio of my ETFs increase due to these new rules?
faq.a: While there might be some compliance costs for AMCs, any impact on expense ratios is typically minimal and would be weighed against the significant benefit of enhanced security and investor confidence. AMCs strive to keep expense ratios competitive.
